claude.sample_unit: treatment plans (40 vignettes each processed twice by two models)
models_evaluated: RAG-LLM (GPT-4o with implant dentistry guideline knowledge base)

links.outcome: Evidence traceability and citation precision of RAG-LLM versus standard LLM in implant treatment plans
links.effect: RAG-LLM significantly outperformed standard model in evidence traceability and citation precision (P = 0.046); overall clinical accuracy showed no significant difference (P = 0.642).
links.quote: However, domain-specific analysis revealed that the RAG-LLM significantly outperformed the standard model in evidence traceability and citation precision (P = 0.046).

links.outcome: Fabricated or misattributed literature citations in generated treatment plans
links.effect: Neither model exhibited severe literature fabrication.
links.quote: Neither model exhibited severe literature fabrication.

links.outcome: Reproducibility across repeated runs (intra-model agreement, diagnostic shifts)
links.effect: High intra-model consistency by weighted Cohen's kappa; severe diagnostic shifts exceedingly rare.
links.quote: Implementing RAG significantly improves evidence traceability, enhances citation precision, and demonstrates high intra-model consistency, with severe diagnostic shifts being exceedingly rare.

links.outcome: RAG retrieval bias causing inappropriate recommendations requiring expert verification
links.effect: RAG showed retrieval bias in soft-tissue complication scenarios, leading to inappropriate hard-tissue augmentation (overtreatment); standard LLM superior in biomechanical spatial planning (P = 0.025).
links.quote: The RAG architecture exhibited "retrieval bias" in soft-tissue complication scenarios, leading to inappropriate hard-tissue augmentation.

links.outcome: Clinical accuracy of AI treatment plans against guidelines across five clinical domains
links.effect: No significant overall accuracy difference (P = 0.642); RAG advantage diminished in out-of-distribution synthetic cases; standard LLM better in spatial planning (P = 0.025).
links.quote: Overall clinical accuracy showed no significant difference between models (P = 0.642).

unlisted_practices: Retrieval bias and out-of-distribution performance of RAG relative to knowledge base thematic coverage

screen.reason: The study directly compares an existing base model (GPT-4o) with and without retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounding on clinical guidelines across standardized clinical vignettes, evaluating citation precision, clinical accuracy, and retrieval bias.
